attempts.label: DANDI:001065
attempts.paper_title: Areal specializations in the morpho-electric and transcriptomic properties of primate layer 5 extratelencephalic projection neurons
attempts.entry_title: Morpho-electric specializations of macaque L5 ET neurons (Dembrow, Sawchuk et al. 2024)
attempts.summary: The core electrophysiology held up. L5 ET neurons had higher resonant frequency, lower input resistance and faster spikes than other cells, and motor cortex differed from temporal cortex in resonance, afterhyperpolarization and input resistance. The transcriptomic findings could not be tested because the sequencing data are not in the dataset and were not processed in the run. Corticospinal neurons grouping with L5 ET cells in the physiology map did not reproduce, nor did the ranking of resonance and input resistance as the largest effects. Classifier and subthreshold oscillation findings held only in part, the latter on a pipeline rebuilt without the authors' code. Spike-width ratio and rheobase claims failed.
attempts.description: Tests the physiology findings of Dembrow, Sawchuk et al. (2024) on dandiset 001065, which holds the current clamp recordings of 294 deep-layer neurons of macaque motor and temporal cortex. Features are computed from the traces; area, preparation and subclass labels come from the paper's per-cell tables on Zenodo. It compares L5 ET with other neurons, L5 ET neurons of the two areas, firing to 4 nA, irregular firing and subthreshold oscillations, and tests the dendritic findings on the paper's deposited morphology features.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Dembrow, Sawchuk et al. (2024) from dandiset 001065

outcomes.notes: All 294 files match a row of L5_physiology_121223.csv by cell name; 47 of its 341 rows are not in the dataset. Donor agrees for 293 of 294 cells and species for 292 of 294 (99.3%). The median Spearman correlation over the 39 features computed here against the table's values is 0.957, with 28 of 39 features at 0.9 or more; the lowest are i_max_gain (0.33), initial_ifreq_gain (0.47) and initial_gain (0.63), and SFA correlates at -0.989 as the table holds the inverse ratio. After the sweep check, maximum and steady-state input resistance agree with the table at Pearson r 0.993 and 0.990. All 68 cells of MCx.pkl and TCx.pkl have a 200 pA series in the files; 7 have exactly the pickle's steps, and the maximum spike counts of 67 of 68 are within 10% of the pickle's (Spearman 0.996). The link holds for the cells in the dataset; 47 cells of the paper's table cannot be linked as they are absent.
deviations: All features are computed here from the traces, as the paper's extraction code was not deposited, with the definitions of STAR Methods and the standard choices named in the claims file and the helper (peak and steady-state windows, linear range of the V-I relation, averaged chirp profiles, fAHP window, spike detection, filtering). Added after verification round 1, a sweep check of the 1 s hyperpolarizing steps (a sweep must hyperpolarize, from a baseline below -40 mV, with the voltage below -20 mV in the step; 13 sweeps of 10 cells rejected) and a chirp check (a profile with no 3 dB cutoff after its maximum is left out; 1 cell), standard choices of this attempt.

outcomes.notes: 27 of 39 features have a BH-corrected projection effect. The largest effect sizes are resonant frequency (0.409), min dV/dt (0.381) and min dV/dt of the 3 ms step spike (0.341); maximum input resistance is fourth (0.332), steady-state input resistance seventh and the 3 dB cutoff eleventh, so one named feature is in the top three and the cutoff is not in the top five. The paper's own table values for the same 294 cells give the same failure (Fr first, min dV/dt second, MaxRn third, cutoff tenth), so it comes from the cells in the dataset or the paper's ranking, not from the extraction here. On ranks of the values computed here (a variant) MaxRn, SSRn, MaxZ and Fr lead and the cutoff is sixth.

outcomes.notes: Species from the files' NCBI taxon (35 M. mulatta cells from 9 subjects, 259 M. nemestrina). No M. mulatta cell comes from acute MCx slices, and under reading (b) several subclasses have 0 to 2 M. mulatta cells, so the four-way model with all interactions is rank deficient (rank 14 of 16 columns under reading a, 29 of 56 under reading b). With type II sums of squares computed from nested least-squares fits, valid on such a design, no feature has a species effect at BH-corrected p < 0.05 under either reading (smallest uncorrected p 0.054, Fr, reading a; 0.041, max_ifreq_gain, reading b; uncorrected p < 0.05 for 0 and 2 features). The additive model (variant) agrees (smallest p 0.067 and 0.11). statsmodels' type II table on the rank-deficient design gives 13 features under reading (a) and 2 under reading (b) (round 1, before the feature checks, 11 and 1); those sums of squares come from aliased columns.

outcomes.notes: Dendrite length per cortical layer needs the reconstructions in the Brain Image Library (doi:10.35077/g.1160) aligned to layer boundaries. The columns of the deposited RawFeatureWide.csv, printed in the notebook, hold no per-layer length (only three apical depth PCs and soma depth from pia), so the claim cannot be tested from them. Fetching and aligning the reconstructions was not attempted within this run's time limit.

All four features differ at BH-corrected p < 0.05 in the stated direction, the criterion's rule, with longer read as the maximum basal path distance (p 0.0095, d 1.94), horizontal extent (0.0015, d 2.79), apical branches (0.017, d 1.64) and maximum apical branch order (0.0054, d 2.11). Total basal length (the other reading of longer) does not differ (0.48). The d values of extent and branches are within tolerance; those of length (1.94 against 2.22) and branch order (2.11 against 1.55) are not, a comparison the criterion reports without making it decide. The deposited notebook printed the same extent and branch order d (2.79, 2.11), as the claims file notes.
deviations: The paper's deposited features of 19 reconstructions are used, not the 23 reconstructions themselves.

outcomes.notes: MCx frequency rises with membrane potential by autocorrelation (r = 0.53, r squared 0.284, p = 1.2e-5, 60 observations from 45 cells) and by the spline FFT peak (r = 0.53, r squared 0.282, p = 3.7e-6, 67 observations from 53 cells; one spline per cell and bin, r squared 0.276, p = 2.1e-6). TCx FFT shows no relation (p = 0.75; 0.21 per cell and bin), but the TCx autocorrelation frequency falls with membrane potential (r = -0.32, p = 0.028), so one of the four conditions fails; the criterion has no partial rule, and partially reproduced is used as three of four hold. The autocorrelation r squared is within tolerance; the FFT r squared is outside 0.288 to 0.352 under both spline readings. The spline maximum lies at 3 to 3.5 Hz, the band's lower edge, in 52% of sweeps, and the largest interior maximum (variant) has no relation with membrane potential in MCx (r = -0.04, p = 0.77), so the FFT result may reflect low-frequency power. Observation counts are below the legend's (79 and 91 in MCx).

The oscillation analysis was R code that was not deposited. It is rebuilt from STAR Methods with the standard choices the claims file names (exponential fit from the AHP trough, baseline within 1 mV of its asymptote, zero-phase 4th-order Butterworth 3 to 50 Hz, autocorrelogram frequency from its first peak). The sweep's FFT peak frequency and strength are the maximum of a smoothing spline fitted to the pooled spectra of its segments (STAR Methods; Figure 7G legend), with the smoothing chosen by generalized cross-validation as R smooth.spline does (the claims file's standard choice); one spline per cell and 5 mV bin is run as a second reading. Strength is the amplitude of the Hann-windowed spectrum (mV), and the trace is resampled to 1 kHz. These are assumed; the paper does not fix them. In round 1 the spline was replaced by the mean of the segments' peaks; that is now a variant.

outcomes.notes: The strength of the spline maximum does not rise with membrane potential in MCx (r = -0.002, p = 0.99, 67 observations; one spline per cell and bin r = 0.008, p = 0.94); TCx r = 0.24, p = 0.083. No variant (interior maximum, mean of the segments' peaks, segments without a spline) has an MCx p below 0.3. Strength is the amplitude of the windowed spectrum, which the paper does not define further.

All features are computed here from the traces, as the paper's extraction code was not deposited, with the definitions of STAR Methods and the standard choices named in the claims file and the helper (peak and steady-state windows, linear range of the V-I relation, averaged chirp profiles, fAHP window, spike detection, filtering). Added after verification round 1, a sweep check of the 1 s hyperpolarizing steps (a sweep must hyperpolarize, from a baseline below -40 mV, with the voltage below -20 mV in the step; 13 sweeps of 10 cells rejected) and a chirp check (a profile with no 3 dB cutoff after its maximum is left out; 1 cell), standard choices of this attempt.
Assumed that Figure S7G, part of the oscillation analysis, uses the sweeps that STAR Methods admit to it (at least one spike and no more than 200); without that limit the claim fails.

findings.statement: The files carry no cortical area, brain region, slice preparation (acute or culture), transcriptomic or predicted subclass, retrograde label or drug condition, and session_description is a placeholder. These come only from the per-cell tables of the paper's code on Zenodo, matched by the electrode cell_id, which every file has. For the 51 L5 ET cells the table lists with synaptic blockers, only one file records when they were applied (cell QN23.26.013.4A.05.01, user comment "started washon of synaptic block" at sweep 91, after 13 of its 10 s sweeps); no other user comment, sweep comment or lab notebook text mentions a blocker or a wash, so for the other 50 cells when blockers were applied cannot be read from the files.

47 of the 341 cells of the code's L5 physiology table (35 of them recorded by one user) are not in the dandiset, which holds 294; the paper reports 333 cells in its physiology analysis, 33 of them from earlier studies.

File sub-Q19-26-009 (cell Q19.26.009.2A.04.02) names subject Q19.26.009 where the paper's table gives donor Q19.26.012, and the two files of subject Q19.01.001 give Macaca mulatta (NCBITaxon 9544) where the table gives M. nemestrina.

One subject has sex U and subject Q19.01.001 has age P1Y/ (1 year, in a malformed ISO duration), where the paper reports animals of 2 to 19 years; the files hold 57 subjects, 22 male, 34 female, against the paper's 58, 23 and 35.

Five files hold 1 s current command steps above 4 nA (up to 16 nA) in their 200 pA series, beyond the 4 nA that STAR Methods give as the headstage limit; whether these currents were delivered is not stated.

Files hold several runs of each protocol (repeats, series stopped early, a 50 pA and a 200 pA series, runs before and after drug application) and nothing marks which sweeps the paper's features use. For 61 of the 68 cells of the 4 nA analysis the steps in the files differ from those of the code's pickles.

Question for the authors. Were the random training splits of the logistic regression classifiers (Figure 3E to 3G and 5E) stratified by class, and with what regularization? predict_subclass was not deposited. Here the weighted f1 holding out 50% is 78.3% (stratified) or 77.5% (unstratified), against 87.9%.

Question for the authors. How were the subthreshold oscillations of Figure 7 and S7 computed (the curve fitted to find the return to baseline after the AHP, the filter, the smoothing of the spline, the measure of strength, and which sweeps enter Figure S7G)? The R code was not deposited. Rebuilt from the Methods with a smoothing spline over each sweep's segment spectra, the MCx frequency rises with membrane potential as reported, but the spline maximum lies at the 3 Hz edge of the band in 52% of sweeps, oscillation strength does not rise with membrane potential, and the TCx autocorrelation frequency falls with membrane potential.

Question for the authors. Which sweeps of each protocol were used for the features, and how were threshold and half-width of late spikes in the 4 nA trains measured? The extraction code was not deposited; the per-step outputs in MCx.pkl carry the names of the Allen Institute's IPFX. The last-to-first half-width ratio in TCx is 1.55 with the Methods' definition and 2.84 with IPFX's width here, against 2.27 in the code's pickle.
The paper's table holds SFA as the last ISI over the second, the inverse of the STAR Methods' ratio of the second ISI to the last (Spearman -0.989 with the Methods' ratio computed here).

The Figure 6D and 6E legend says TCx L5 ET neurons have a deeper fast AHP and more symmetrical spikes than MCx ones; the Results and the code's means say the opposite, and the data here agree with the Results (fAHP -15.9 against -11.4 mV, up/down ratio 2.69 against 3.31, MCx against TCx).
The paper's deposited morphology features (RawFeatureWide.csv) cover 19 reconstructions, 10 MCx and 9 TCx, where the paper reports 12 and 11.

In 10 files the first run of 1 s hyperpolarizing steps holds sweeps that do not hyperpolarize the cell, start from a baseline above -40 mV or reach -20 mV (13 sweeps; some read 0 mV, as from a lost recording), and nothing in the files marks them. Used as they are, they gave negative steady-state input resistances for 3 cells.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier queried the archive metadata and tested helper functions on synthetic inputs. Its report had no attempt record and gave its own outcome for each of the 42 claims; 41 agree with the record and one (fig5c-basal-apical-features) does not.

disagreements.reason: Max path distance, extent_x, apical branches and apical max branch order all have BH p < 0.05 in the stated direction. Two d values are outside tolerance (1.94 against 2.22; 2.11 against 1.55), but under the criterion d does not decide the outcome. Total length (another reading of "longer") is not significant.

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the round 1 revision, with its conclusions and summary, the helper module, the claims file, the attempt record and the entry README, with the paper. The verifier tested anova_estimable on synthetic data. It agrees with all 42 outcomes and found the six assumptions stated and reasonable.

entries.name: 001065-dembrow-2024
entries.title: Morpho-electric specializations of macaque L5 ET neurons (Dembrow, Sawchuk et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the physiology findings of Dembrow, Sawchuk et al. (2024) on dandiset 001065, which holds the current clamp recordings of 294 deep-layer neurons of macaque motor and temporal cortex. Features are computed from the traces; area, preparation and subclass labels come from the paper's per-cell tables on Zenodo. It compares L5 ET with other neurons, L5 ET neurons of the two areas, firing to 4 nA, irregular firing and subthreshold oscillations, and tests the dendritic findings on the paper's deposited morphology features.
